text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chairman of parliament's foreign affairs committee says shocked by Bahraini members of the al-Shoura legislative council visit to Iraqi President's son Uday.
- A Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) panel considers further selloffs of state holdings in local firms.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives message from Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
- Cabinet approves a two-year prison penalty and a 2,000-dinar ($6,600) fine for prank callers.
- Britain's Prince Charles says invest in young people. Prince Charles left Kuwait for Bahrian late on Saturday after a two-day official visiti to the Gulf Arab state.
- Canadian minister of national defence starts Kuwait visit.
- Light weapons found at a power station in a Kuwait City suburb. Iraqi occupation troops left large amounts of weapons and ammunition as they fled Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
- Kuwait offers condolences to China over the death of Deng Xiaoping.
